passages.title: Cyrus permits return
passages.summary: Cyrus announces temple rebuilding. Families prepare to return, and Sheshbazzar receives the temple vessels. Neighbors give gold, animals, and supplies. Their gifts help families prepare for the return.

passages.summary: A list names returning families and temple workers. Some priests must prove their family line. Families name their earlier homes. Priests without proof must wait before eating the most holy food.
passages.dateLabel: Chapter order · Persian reign sequence requires comparison
passages.uncertainty: Selected known places and broad regions. Ahava, Casiphia, and the archive destination are not assigned unsupported coordinates.

passages.title: Altar, foundations, joy, and grief
passages.summary: Jeshua and Zerubbabel lead renewed offerings and temple work. The foundation ceremony brings both celebration and grief. Older people remember the earlier temple and weep. Others cheer as the new foundation is laid.
passages.dateLabel: Chapter order · Persian reign sequence requires comparison
passages.uncertainty: Selected known places and broad regions. Ahava, Casiphia, and the archive destination are not assigned unsupported coordinates.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me considers the joy and grief accompanying temple rebuilding.

passages.title: Opposition and royal letters
passages.summary: An offer of help is rejected. Opposition and letters to Persian rulers interrupt rebuilding before work resumes under Darius. The chapter moves between different kings. Some later letters concern the city's walls instead of temple work.
passages.dateLabel: Chapter order · Persian reign sequence requires comparison
passages.uncertainty: Selected known places and broad regions. Ahava, Casiphia, and the archive destination are not assigned unsupported coordinates.

passages.title: Prophets encourage work as officials ask questions
passages.summary: Haggai and Zechariah encourage rebuilding. Tattenai asks for proof of Cyrus's order, and the leaders explain their work. The builders recall Sheshbazzar's earlier foundation work. Officials seek written proof of the king's permission.

passages.title: Ezra studies the law and receives royal support
passages.summary: Ezra is a priest who studies God’s law. Artaxerxes supports his journey and gives him duties to teach and judge. Ezra studies the law before living and teaching it. His journey connects these duties with the returning community.
passages.dateLabel: Chapter order · Persian reign sequence requires comparison
passages.uncertainty: Selected known places and broad regions. Ahava, Casiphia, and the archive destination are not assigned unsupported coordinates.

lds.text: The Church lesson joins scripture study with practice and teaching.

passages.title: Prayer, travel, and the care of temple gifts
passages.summary: Ezra gathers travelers and asks Iddo to send temple workers. They pray before leaving and count the gifts when they arrive. Ezra chooses people to guard the gifts. They must hand over the same weight they received.
passages.dateLabel: Chapter order · Persian reign sequence requires comparison
passages.uncertainty: Selected known places and broad regions. Ahava, Casiphia, and the archive destination are not assigned unsupported coordinates.

lds.text: The Seminary lesson studies fasting, prayer, and trust before the journey.

passages.title: Ezra prays about the mixed marriages
passages.summary: Leaders report marriages with women from other nations. Ezra tears his robe and begins a prayer. Ezra recalls earlier sins that sent Israel into exile. He fears losing the small group that survived.
passages.dateLabel: Chapter order · Persian reign sequence requires comparison
